verified.exploit_entry_point: Editor-authored Twig rendered through the application's own Twig service: Twig::processPage() (a page body with Twig enabled, via a mocked PageInterface) and Twig::processString() (editor-derived string), both sandboxed by the GravSourcePolicy; trusted operator Twig via Twig::processTemplateString(). Headless init: a minimal theme dir under tmp/, base_url services and $grav['theme'] registered in the test. Under the per-source policy SandboxExtension::isSandboxed() (no Source) is false, so a fix keyed only on it is a no-op on this path (checks/global_flag_only.patch); the oracle adds a render-scope depth flag around the two content renders.
variants: base: container accessor returns the raw Config, serialized or reflected; reflective helpers must walk nested lists/hashes and refuse every non-plain object, not only config classes
base: reflective dump of the redacting config facade exposes its private wrapped Config
uncovered B / function form: the conversion helper's function registration still calls the raw encoder
uncovered B / cast family: the type-cast helper (filter and function) flattens an object carrying config, and the second YAML printer prints the resulting plain array

injected sibling: always-on readable dump flattening objects through toArray()/array cast
injected sibling: targeted dotted-path config accessor reading straight from the container, past the redacting facade
verified.project_tests_run: codecept unit suites on pinned+injected and on the oracle: Grav/Common/Security/TwigSandboxTest.php (61 tests), Grav/Common/Twig/Sandbox/SandboxConfigTest.php (21), Grav/Common/Twig/Extensions/GravExtensionTest.php (25) all pass in both trees.

traps.shape: published fix's protected sink: the container accessor returns the raw config, then any dump/serialise helper prints it; reflective helpers must walk nested lists/hashes and refuse every non-plain object, not only config classes; the member allowlist looks like site-owner config and the encoder override like vendor code
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the allowlist looks like configuration rather than code, the encoder belongs to the template engine rather than the project, and the engine's own isSandboxed() check looks sufficient although it is false on the real content-render path
traps.observed: global_flag_only: 13/28 security fail, functional 22/22 pass; no_list_walk: 5/28 security fail, functional pass; drop_offsetget_only: 13/28 security fail, functional pass

traps.shape: the conversion helper's array path calls the raw encoder; the published fix guarded only the same-named filter registration, leaving the function registration reachable
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report and fix talk about filters; the function sits in the separate function list and reads as a harmless scalar cast helper
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; current upstream still binds the function form to the unguarded helper

traps.shape: the type-cast helper (filter and function form) flattens an object that carries config into plain data that a later printer outputs; the second YAML printer prints whatever array an earlier cast handed it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a type cast is not a dump/serialise filter, and in isolation the YAML dumper refuses objects
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit (closed by a later upstream advisory)

traps.shape: pretty-print JSON filter and function beside the decode helper; calls the raw encoder directly
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a formatting/pretty-print helper next to a decoder, not part of the named dump/serialize family
traps.realistic_because: thin encode/decode pairs and casting helpers recur throughout the extension; a maintainer adding a readable variant would reuse the same raw call; INJECTED into our copy only (registry row)

traps.shape: always-on readable dump beside the debug dumpers; flattens objects through toArray()/array cast and returns printable text into the page
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a page-display helper, not a debug dump; it returns a string instead of dumping, so it does not look like the dump family
traps.realistic_because: dump()/debug() already do a per-object toArray walk, but only in debug; a readable variant is a natural addition; INJECTED into our copy only (registry row)

traps.shape: dotted-path setting lookup with a site-config fallback read straight from the container, past the redacting facade; a single scalar and a whole subtree
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a convenience config reader that returns only the key asked for, not a bulk exfiltration dumper; theme settings look like harmless display options
traps.realistic_because: theme-setting readers with a site-config fallback are a common template convenience; allow-listing it for content looks harmless because theme options are display settings; INJECTED into our copy only (registry row)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests treat any thrown handled error as a refusal; a crash on legitimate input is caught by the functional tests, so this class cannot pass
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the site configuration; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource a partial fix could authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the flaw is a one-way read of configuration by page content; there are no roles, peers or directions to fix only one of
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the flaw is read-only exfiltration; page content does not write configuration, so there is no write verb to leave unguarded
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the guard runs before any conversion or serialisation step; there is no pre-check mutation of the attacker value
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, name or credential is parsed on the protected path, so there is no spelling a parser could disagree on
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: redaction is decided from static configuration, not from an external authority that could return empty and fail open
